title: Colts vs. Vikings Live Score & Stats: October 25, 2026 GameTracker Update on CBS Sports
body:
The Minnesota Vikings rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Indianapolis Colts 27‑20 on Sunday night, clinching a pivotal victory that keeps their playoff aspirations alive and underscores a defense that has finally found its identity this season. Safety Harrison Smith delivered the decisive blow with a late‑fourth‑quarter interception that sealed the win, capping a performance that highlighted Minnesota’s resurgence after a sluggish start and confirming the Vikings’ ability to win in hostile territory.

From the opening kickoff, the Colts appeared to have the upper hand, converting a sustained drive into a 3‑point field goal and then adding a 12‑yard rushing touchdown by Jonathan Taylor to take a 10‑0 lead. Indianapolis’ balanced attack, blending Taylor’s ground game with quarterback Anthony Richardson’s deep throws, seemed poised to keep the Vikings on the back foot. However, Minnesota’s offensive coordinator Jeff Fisher made a critical adjustment at halftime, shifting the focus to quick, high‑percentage passes that exploited gaps in the Colts’ secondary. The change paid immediate dividends as quarterback Kirk Cousins connected with wideout Justin Jefferson for a 45‑yard strike, setting up a 7‑yard touchdown run by Dalvin Cook that narrowed the margin to 10‑7.

The second half turned into a chess match between the two coaching staffs. The Vikings’ defense, which had been porous in the first quarter, began to tighten its coverage and apply relentless pressure on Richardson. Defensive end Danielle Hunter recorded a sack and forced a fumble that set up a short field for Minnesota, leading to a 23‑13 lead after a 12‑yard touchdown pass to tight end T.J. Hockenson. The Colts responded with a quick drive of their own, highlighted by a 30‑yard completion to Michael Thomas, but a missed extra point left them trailing 23‑19.

As the clock wound down, the game’s tension heightened. Richardson engineered a methodical drive that brought Indianapolis within three points, but a crucial third‑down stop by the Vikings’ secondary forced a punt. The Colts’ final possession was a gamble: Richardson attempted a deep pass to tight end Dalton Schultz, only to have Smith read the route perfectly and step in front of the receiver for the game‑sealing interception. Smith’s pick not only halted the Colts’ comeback hopes but also cemented his status as a defensive leader, marking his third interception of the season and his first in a high‑stakes road win.

Beyond the final score, the victory carries significant implications for both franchises. For Minnesota, the win improves their record to 5‑2, positioning them firmly in the NFC North race and providing momentum heading into a critical stretch of divisional games. The defensive turnaround—evident in the reduction of yards allowed from 380 in the first half to just 150 in the second—suggests that the coaching staff’s emphasis on aggressive play‑calling is bearing fruit. Meanwhile, the Colts, now 4‑3, must address their inability to close out games when trailing. Richardson’s poise under pressure remains a bright spot, but the offensive line’s failure to protect him on crucial third downs exposed a vulnerability that opponents will likely exploit in the weeks ahead.

Looking ahead, the Vikings will travel to Green Bay next Sunday, where a win would give them a three‑game lead in the division and further solidify their status as NFC contenders. The Colts, on the other hand, return home to face the Jacksonville Jaguars, a matchup that could serve as a litmus test for their resilience after a disappointing loss. Both teams have clear pathways to the postseason, but the margin for error is shrinking. Minnesota’s blend of veteran savvy and emerging talent, anchored by a defense that finally appears cohesive, may be the catalyst they need to sustain a deep playoff run. Indianapolis must translate Richardson’s flashes of brilliance into consistent production if they hope to remain competitive in a crowded AFC South. The season is far from over, and each week will bring new challenges that could redefine the trajectories set in motion on this pivotal night in Indianapolis.
